New Dodge Hyper-Muscle Concept Wants To Steal the SRT Copperhead’s Thunder – Rendering
7 photos
Photo: Instagram | adry53customs
What’s the least exciting muscle car that money can buy today? Some might argue it’s the EcoBoost-powered S650 Ford Mustang , whereas other would say it is none other than the modern-day Dodge Charger.
Why the latter? Because while the former model can be specified with a V8 engine, the Charger cannot. And that’s despite the fact that it will blow two candles off its birthday cake at the end of the year. Production started in late 2024 at the Windsor factory in Ontario, Canada. Both body styles, the coupe and sedan, are based on the STLA Large (Longitudinal) platform, meaning that they share their nuts and bolts with the upcoming Stelvio and Giulia from Alfa Romeo, and the second-gen Maserati Levante.
But fret not, fellow gearhead, because while Dodge’s initial bet was on straight-six twin-turbocharged and electric firepower when it comes to the new-age Charger , the company admitted it was wrong not to launch this model with a V8. After all, multiple reviewers have said that it behaves like something that would feature a V8, and Dodge is now ready to take this step, with the rumor mill speaking about it hitting the assembly line at the end of 2027, and launching as a 2028 model year at dealers nationwide.
Hemi V8 firepower is therefore a thing, apparently, and word on the street is that it will be none other than the 6.2-liter supercharged V8 that might power this model. The Hellcat lump makes over 700 horsepower in its base configuration and more than 800 horsepower on superior models. And in its peak form, it offers 1,025 horsepower in the Dodge Challenger SRT Demon 170, rocketing it to 60 mph in 1.66 seconds, and turning it into an 8.91-second muscle car down the quarter mile, with an exit speed of over 151 mph (243+ kph).
Photo: Instagram | adry53customs Dodge has some bold ideas for its muscle car lineup, as the Copperhead is also in the making, reportedly. The model might get the SRT suffix in the top-of-the-line flavor, and was supposedly teased during the Stellantis Investor Day almost half a year ago, next to the GLH crossover that should utilize the STLA One platform, and could also get an SRT (or more) flavor.
The mysterious muscle car say under wraps in a teaser pic, and it looked very different from the standard Charger lineup. It looks like it has a big rear wing, so it would send Charger Daytona (the classic one, d’oh!) and Plymouth Superbird vibes. It will likely be based on the same platform as the modern-day Charger, and it should launch with V8 firepower, probably under the Dodge Copperhead (SRT) name.
Inspired by everything happening in Dodge’s upcoming lineup , the rendering crowd has already imagined quite a few monstrous-looking Charger-based muscle cars so far. One of the latest to have crossed our screens came from @adry63customs on Instagram. The pixel master dropped a short video of the so-called Dodge Hyper-Muscle Concept that shows it in motion from several angles, and while it is obviously on the very special side of things, it was clearly based on the modern-day Charger.
Photo: Instagram | adry53customs The CGI-infused study features a familiar front end, albeit a different bumper, and a very muscular-looking hood with a cutout for the supercharger. There wheel arches have been enlarged, the door mirrors are very slim, the back end is home to an intricate-looking diffuser and a ducktail spoiler, and we can also see that the big wheels are on the very special side of things.
But the icing on the cake lies beneath the skin, as something like this would have a dedicated chassis setup, as well as uprated brakes to keep the extra oomph in check. And the only firepower would be a V8 , with a supercharger assisting it. If we were to dream about it, we’d say that it deserves a four-digit output, though on a more realistic scenario, it would probably take on the Ford Mustang Dark Horse SC or, who knows, maybe the Mustang GTD.
This muscle car is one dark overall look away from tapping into its devilish side, and we’d say that the Hellcat decals on the rear three-quarter panels and rear pillars would be a welcomed addition. But let’s not forget that we are looking at a virtual study that lives its life in Fantasy Land, and has absolutely nothing in common with the upcoming V8-powered Dodge Charger, which is expected for the 2028 model year as mentioned above, nor the Copperhead, that could be due in 2029 or perhaps 2030.
Now, this CGI model’s overall design is definitely not bad at all, but to be honest, it is not perfect either, as it is a bit on the flashy side of things. But assuming this is what the V8-powered Charger would look like, would you order one over an S650 Ford Mustang with an eight-cylinder engine under the hood?
